title: Left additivity of the dot product under subtraction
statement:
For any three vectors $s, t, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, the dot product is additive in its left argument under subtraction:
\[
(s - t) \cdot x = s \cdot x - t \cdot x,
\]
where the subtraction on the left is taken componentwise and both sides are elements of $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$.
hypotheses_covered: s, t, x are vectors in Z_k^n
replaced:
For $s, t, x \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$,
$(s - t) \cdot x = s \cdot x - t \cdot x$.
